Zambezi Industrial Holdings Enters Liquidation, Casting Uncertainty Over Diversified Industrials Sector in Zambia

LUSAKA – Zambezi Industrial Holdings Plc, one of Zambia’s leading diversified industrial firms, has formally entered liquidation proceedings this week after months of financial distress, company officials confirmed on Thursday. The company, which has operated in the sector for over three decades, has been a major player in the production and supply of a wide range of industrial goods across the country.

The Lusaka High Court appointed Tembwe & Associates as liquidators following a petition filed by Zambezi Industrial Holdings itself, citing unmanageable debt levels and sustained losses. As of Thursday, the company’s facilities in Lusaka, Ndola, and Kitwe have suspended most production lines, with only essential security and maintenance staff remaining on site.

“We deeply regret the disruption this has caused to our operations and our dedicated workforce,” said Chileshe Mumba, interim spokesperson for Zambezi Industrial Holdings. “Despite significant efforts to restructure and attract new investment, market conditions and mounting obligations have made continued operations untenable.”

According to company records, Zambezi Industrial Holdings employed over 620 staff across its facilities as of March 2024. All employees have been notified of the liquidation process, with union representatives advocating for the timely payment of outstanding wages and benefits. “Our priority is to protect the rights and interests of our members during this difficult process,” said Emmanuel Banda, regional secretary for the Industrial Workers Union of Zambia. “We are in direct talks with the liquidators to ensure no worker is left behind.”

The Diversified Industrials Association of Zambia expressed concern about the development, noting that Zambezi Industrial Holdings was a founding member and key contributor to sector growth. “This is a challenging moment for the entire industry,” said Chairperson Lucy Mwale. “We urge all stakeholders to consider the long-term impact and support the transition process for affected employees and facilities.”

Local analysts say the liquidation of such a prominent company signals broader challenges within Zambia’s diversified industrial sector, including rising input costs and limited access to credit. “Zambezi Industrial Holdings’ financial troubles reflect some of the underlying pressures facing the sector,” said Dr. Joseph Simukonda, an industrial economist at the University of Zambia. “The immediate focus will be on winding down operations responsibly and exploring options for asset recovery.”

As liquidation proceedings continue, the company’s remaining assets are expected to be assessed and sold to pay creditors. At the time of writing, the process is ongoing, with no formal announcements regarding the future of the company’s plants or workforce.
